target_customer: Precision hardware manufacturers and contract manufacturers of device components (phones, watches, laptops)
problem: Manual inspection under microscopes misses roughly 15 percent of defects, and traditional machine vision cannot keep up with fast design changes. Hundred scans a whole tray of parts for sub-100 micron defects.
business_model: Benchtop inspection station hardware plus software
product_category: Automated visual inspection for precision parts

founders.name: Iris Liao
education: Imperial College London, MSc Applied Mathematics

competitors.name: UnitX
competitors.what: AI visual inspection, launched Flex system in March 2026 and DeteX smart camera in June 2026

competitors.name: Instrumental
competitors.what: Full stack inspection platform with camera hardware for electronics

technical_complexity.rationale: Custom imaging rig with controlled lighting and models that learn from one good part to detect sub-100 micron defects across materials.

defensibility.rationale: Hardware and workflow integration help, but UnitX, Instrumental and Cognex sell similar inspection.

market_need_then: Defects cost US discrete manufacturers an estimated 45 billion dollars a year per the YC page; manual microscope inspection is still common.

identity.visual_style: Minimal engineering look, uppercase step labels, simple tray illustration
identity.voice_and_tone: Short declarative lines such as 100% inspection the default

branding.brand_signature: 100 percent inspection, tied to the name

brand_strength.rationale: The name matches the 100 percent promise but is common; the site has a tight message and no brand coverage exists.

outcome_analysis: Hundred is a three person F26 company led by a hardware engineer from Meta, Google and Magic Leap, with a software and ML team, building tray-level inspection. No funding beyond YC is public, and it faces established inspection vendors. No outcome events found.
notes: No funding found in two searches; name origin is not stated (the 100 percent link is an inference, not recorded as origin). Competitor sources are 2026 roundups of mixed quality.
